chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: The band's trick to rent a hotel cheaply
summary: The musicians parked the bus away and checked in a few at a time, renting the whole hotel before the owner knew.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters

blocks.x: So what we did, we would get in town and we wouldn't park the bus. We wouldn't go in front of

hotel.
So we would go park the bus like two
blocks down around the corner where nobody in that
neighborhood would know that we were in town.

So we would begin to walk out -- you
know, (inaudible) -- you know, just like we're getting
off from work, have riding (inaudible) clothes on. Suit
Collar all opened (inaudible). We
would walk down to the hotel. "Hey, you got a room?"
"Yeah."
"How much?"
"Oh, a dollar and a half." Two dollars,
you know.
After a while, two more will go in.
"Got any rooms?"
"Yeah."
"Just two of us together."
"Yeah, so and so."
So the girl would be on the desk. So
she wouldn't know what was going on, you know.
Before she find out, we done rented the
whole hotel for a dollar and a half a day, see.
[chuckles]

The guy come back -- this is the God honest truth -- the guy comes downstairs -- the fella that own the hotel, he came (inaudible).
He say, "Did the band get in yet?" He says, "What band? I ain't seen no band."
"You know musicians coming here?" "Well, a lot of fellas been here renting rooms, so I ain't seen no band."
So what we would do is leave the instruments on the bus and the uniforms. Because we could dress --
So Joe Saunders, the road manager would take the things to the ballroom, set up the bandstand and everything.
Take the uniforms to the tailor and have them cleaned and pressed and brought back to the ballroom where we were playing.
And they never saw the band. The band's not in town.
So at nighttime when we got through work, here we come walking in with the instruments in
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

in uniform. our hands (inaudible). He say, "That's the band." He would give the -- I could hear them down there arguing with the man on the desk. "Why you let that band in here, so and so and so?" "We didn't know they were the band." We would be up there just laughing and carrying on, because we would beat them to the gun. Say, "Um hum. Next time we come -- we'll be back here next week, but they know when we come in." We pulled that on a lot of places (inaudible) people who were doing that to us. Chic say So (inaudible), "Park the bus down here and go up and get the room. Don't go all at one time," like, you know, some of us would go to another hotel, some of us go over there. And the people would be looking for the band. "The band come in yet?" Guys come down in the lobby (inaudible). We got to go get something to eat and (inaudible) to the ballroom and check on the instruments and things.

(Inaudible), "Is the band in yet?"
"No, I ain't hear no band."
And we'd be up there -- you know, the whole band would be in the hotel. A dollar and a half a day.
They'd charge us five dollars if they found out we were the band, you know. And they'd be down there arguing like mad.
He'd be giving the girl --
"Did the band come in yet? Who got these rooms?"
We'd come back, we'd go out at a time, two at a time and go to the ballroom.
